AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL
  MAY 16, 2023
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF ASSEMBLY BILL 361,
WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL
LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO:
publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP
WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE
VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.

  CLOSED SESSION MEETING
  5:00 PM

  REGULAR MEETING
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Ana Valencia, Mayor
  Margarita L. Rios, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
 Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter within its
 jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address City
 Council, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms.
 City Council will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. City Council will
 hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency
 or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a
 future City Council meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other
 services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are available at this
 meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
 made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time
 when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the
 meeting or service.

 Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has been posted will also
 be made available for public inspection.

 Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk’s Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular business
 hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the
 City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

 CONSENT CALENDAR

 Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
 Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

1.  MEETING MINUTES
  Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of May 2, 2023.  825-04

2.  PAYROLL FOR THE PERIOD APRIL 16, 2023 – APRIL 29, 2023
  Staff recommends City Council approve gross payroll in the amount of $1,107,720.29; the payroll check
  numbers 37805-37807 and the voucher numbers 318157 – 318611 in the total net amount of $822,392.28
  for the pay period April 16, 2023 – April 29, 2023.  630

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS
  Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period April 25, 2023 – May 8, 2023, in the
  total amount of $3,664,234.92.  640

4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY
  Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Ruben Loza.  810-12

5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS - MAY 10, 2023
  No action is required unless the City Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on
  the item where the Commission’s action was final.  260

 City Council, May 16, 2023  Page 3 of 5
 6.  RESOLUTION NO. 23-27 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  DEPARTMENT
  Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 23-27, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT.  870-02

7.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS
  Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.
  b.  City Council continues to impose or recommend measures to promote social distancing including
  remote or hybrid meeting participation.  825

8.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO 1 - ADVANCED RESERVATION DIAL-A-RIDE / SUBSCRIPTION
  SERVICE
  Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 1 in the amount of $144,256 using Norwalk
  Transportation System operating funds and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment, on
  behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.  1120-07

9.  AUTHORIZATION TO SUBMIT ZERO EMISSIONS BUS ROLLOUT PLAN
  Staff recommends City Council approve the Zero Emissions Bus Rollout Plan and authorize the Executive
  Director of Regional Transportation to submit the plan to the California Air Resources Board by July 1, 2023.
  1130

10. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 1 – THE HEART OF NORWALK SPECIFIC PLAN AND
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT - ADDITIONAL SERVICES
  Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 1 to the agreement with The Arroyo Group for the
  Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan and Environmental Impact Report, for additional services not-to-exceed
  $732,500; and authorize the City Manager to execute this amendment and any additional amendments
  provided there is funding in the budget and it is within his signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney.  325-03

11. RESOLUTION NO. 23-26 – ESTABLISHING AND/OR AMENDING POSTED SPEED LIMITS FOR 81
  STREET SEGMENTS WITHIN THE CITY OF NORWALK – ENGINEER’S REPORT NO. 23-04
  Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  receive and file Engineer’s Report No. 23-04; and
  b.  adopt Resolution No. 23-26, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  CERTIFYING AND ESTABLISING SPEED LIMITS ON CERTAIN STREETS WITHIN CITY.  1050-08

12. PROJECT NO. 7450 - WELL NO. 10 GRANULAR ACTIVATED CARBON TREATMENT AND SYSTEM
  UPGRADES AND PROJECT NO. 7606 – POTTER STREET STORM DRAIN REPAIRS - AWARD
  CONTRACTS FOR PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES FOR DESIGN, ENVIRONMENTAL
  COMPLIANCE, PROJECT MANAGEMENT, AND CONSTRUCTION SUPPORT SERVICES
  Staff recommends City Council approve agreements with:

  a.  Civiltec Engineering, Inc. for Project No. 7450 to provide professional engineering services for design,
  environmental compliance project management, and construction support for Work Order No. 1 for a
  term of two years from the date of execution, with the option to extend for two additional one-year
  term extensions, for an amount not to exceed $295,347; and authorize the City Manager to execute
  the agreement, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by
  the City Attorney; and
  b.  Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc. for Project No. 7606 to provide professional engineering services
  for design, project management, and construction support for Work Order No. 2 for a term of two
  years from the date of execution, with the option to extend for two additional one-year term

  agreement, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the
  City Attorney.  1005-04-7450/7606

13. CONFIRM EMERGENCY WORK AT 11907 168TH STREET AND 16331 ALORA AVENUE
  Staff recommends City Council confirm the emergency service repair work at 11907 168th Street and 16331
  Alora Avenue, completed by Stephen Doreck Equipment Rentals, Inc., in the amount of $14,084.16.  955

APPOINTMENTS

14. ADVISORY BODY APPOINTMENTS
  Staff recommends City Councilmembers make appointments to fill the vacancies on the various Advisory
  Bodies for two-year terms expiring on December 31, 2024.  200

REPORTS

  Receive and file.  920

  Staff recommends City Council receive and file.  325

ADJOURNMENT

Theresa Devoy, CMC
